questions.prompt: The eigenvalues of the system matrix \(A\) determine
options: the modes of the free response
questions.explanation: Each eigenvalue gives a mode: exponential decay for real negative, oscillation for complex pairs. The eigenvectors determine how much each initial condition excites each mode. \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\) affect forced response and output, not the natural modes.

questions.prompt: A 2x2 diagonal matrix has entries \([-2, -5]\). The slower eigenvalue is
questions.explanation: The eigenvalue \(-2\) is closer to zero than \(-5\), so it decays more slowly. The time constant of the slow mode is \(1/2 = 0.5\) s. The fast mode has time constant \(1/5 = 0.2\) s.

questions.prompt: Same matrix. The time constant of the fast mode is
questions.explanation: The fast eigenvalue is \(-5\). The time constant is \(\tau = 1/|-5| = 0.2\) s. After \(0.2\) s, this mode decays by \(e^{-1}\).

questions.prompt: A complex eigenvalue \(\lambda = -1 + 2j\) contributes a mode that
questions.explanation: The real part \(-1\) gives exponential decay. The imaginary part \(\pm 2\) gives oscillation at 2 rad/s. The conjugate pair together produce a real-valued damped sinusoid.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>complex eigenvalue</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="123" y1="41" x2="133" y2="51" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="51" x2="133" y2="41" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="129" x2="133" y2="139" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="139" x2="133" y2="129" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>
questions.figure_alt: Pole marks in the complex plane.

questions.prompt: A complex eigenvalue is \(-3 + 4j\). The natural frequency (distance to origin) is
questions.explanation: \(\omega_n = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\) rad/s. The damping ratio is \(\zeta = 3/5 = 0.6\). The decay rate is the real part, 3.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>natural frequency</title><line x1="20" y1="92" x2="280" y2="92"/><polygon points="280,92 273.6,94.7 273.6,89.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="164" y1="160" x2="164" y2="16"/><polygon points="164,16 166.7,22.4 161.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="172" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="117" y1="31" x2="127" y2="41" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="117" y1="41" x2="127" y2="31" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="117" y1="143" x2="127" y2="153" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="117" y1="153" x2="127" y2="143" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>
questions.figure_alt: Pole marks in the complex plane.

questions.prompt: Same eigenvalue, \(-3 + 4j\). The damping ratio is
questions.explanation: The damping ratio is \(\zeta = |\mathrm{Re}|/\omega_n = 3/5 = 0.6\). This is the cosine of the angle from the negative real axis to the pole.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>damping ratio</title><line x1="20" y1="92" x2="280" y2="92"/><polygon points="280,92 273.6,94.7 273.6,89.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="164" y1="160" x2="164" y2="16"/><polygon points="164,16 166.7,22.4 161.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="172" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="117" y1="31" x2="127" y2="41" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="117" y1="41" x2="127" y2="31" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="117" y1="143" x2="127" y2="153" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="117" y1="153" x2="127" y2="143" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>
questions.figure_alt: Pole marks in the complex plane.

questions.prompt: The matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}\) is upper triangular. Its eigenvalues are
questions.explanation: For a triangular matrix, the eigenvalues are the diagonal entries: \(-1\) and \(-3\). No characteristic polynomial is needed. The faster answer asks for one eigenvalue; \(-1\) is the slower.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>triangular eigenvalues</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="70" y2="90"/><line x1="98" y1="90" x2="114" y2="90"/><line x1="142" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="123" y1="85" x2="133" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="95" x2="133" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="85" x2="89" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="95" x2="89" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>
questions.figure_alt: Pole marks in the complex plane.

questions.prompt: Same matrix. If the initial state is \([1, 0]^T\), which is an eigenvector for \(\lambda = -1\), the state at \(t = 1\) is entirely in the first mode with value
questions.explanation: Starting on an eigenvector, only that mode is excited: \(x_1(t) = e^{-t}\). At \(t = 1\), \(x_1 = e^{-1} = 0.368\). The second mode is not excited.
questions.figure_alt: A curve that decays toward zero.

questions.prompt: If \(A\) is diagonalizable as \(A = V \Lambda V^{-1}\), the matrix exponential is
questions.explanation: Diagonalization gives \(e^{At} = V e^{\Lambda t} V^{-1}\), where \(e^{\Lambda t}\) is diagonal with entries \(e^{\lambda_i t}\). This is the standard formula for computing the matrix exponential.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>diagonal exponential</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">e^{\lambda_1 t}   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">0   e^{\lambda_2 t}</text></svg>

questions.prompt: A realization has eigenvalues \(-0.5\), \(-2\), and \(-4\). After 10 s, the response is dominated by the slowest mode. The dominant eigenvalue is
questions.explanation: The eigenvalue \(-0.5\) has time constant 2 s. After 10 s (5 time constants), the other modes are negligible. The slow mode dominates the long-term response.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>dominant mode</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="48" y2="90"/><line x1="76" y1="90" x2="92" y2="90"/><line x1="120" y1="90" x2="125" y2="90"/><line x1="153" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="134" y1="85" x2="144" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="134" y1="95" x2="144" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="85" x2="111" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="95" x2="111" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="57" y1="85" x2="67" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="57" y1="95" x2="67" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: The trace of a 2x2 matrix with eigenvalues \(-1\) and \(-4\) is
questions.explanation: The trace equals the sum of eigenvalues: \(-1 + (-4) = -5\). The determinant is the product: \((-1)(-4) = 4\). These are the invariants of the characteristic polynomial.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>trace and determinant</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">-1   ?</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">?   -4</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A matrix with diagonal entries shown.

questions.prompt: For observability: if a mode is unobservable,
options: the mode cannot be excited by input
the mode determines the DC gain
the mode cannot be seen at the output
questions.explanation: An unobservable mode does not appear in the output regardless of initial conditions. It may still evolve internally. An uncontrollable mode cannot be excited by input. These are dual concepts.
